tiles.Bank Nifty: The banking index. Banks are a big part of the Indian market, so this box moves a lot of weight.
tiles.Brent: Brent crude, the oil price most of the world — including India — uses as a reference.
tiles.Copper: Copper, in dollars per pound. Widely used in wiring and construction.
tiles.Crude WTI: Crude oil, in dollars per barrel. India imports most of its oil, so this box matters.
tiles.Dow: 30 famous large US companies. One of the oldest indices in the world.
tiles.Gold: Gold, priced in US dollars per ounce. Often seen as a safe asset when people are worried.
tiles.India VIX: The fear gauge. It shows how much movement traders expect in the Nifty over the next 30 days. It is not a market you invest in — it only shows the mood.
tiles.Nasdaq: US tech-heavy index. A strong green day in America lifts this box.
tiles.Natural Gas: US natural gas, used for heating and power. A small box on this map.
tiles.Nifty 50: India's main index — 50 big companies. When it is green, the broad market had a good day.
tiles.Nifty Auto: Car, two-wheeler and auto-parts makers. It shows how much people are buying vehicles.
tiles.Nifty IT: IT companies — software and services. Sensitive to the US economy and the rupee.
tiles.Nifty Metal: Steel, aluminium, copper and mining companies. It follows global metal prices.
tiles.Nifty Pharma: Medicine and healthcare makers. Many earn a large share of their money from exports.
tiles.S&P 500: 500 big American companies. The main US benchmark — like Nifty 50 is for India.
tiles.Sensex: 30 large companies on the Bombay Stock Exchange. India's oldest index.
tiles.Silver: Silver, priced in US dollars per ounce. Used in jewellery and in industry.
tiles.USD/INR: How many rupees one US dollar buys. A higher number means a weaker rupee.

tour.text: Green means up, red means down. A green box went up today; a red box went down. The darker the colour, the bigger the move. This gold-outlined box moved the most today.

Bigger box, bigger market. Each box is sized by how big that market is. Nifty 50 is the biggest box — it tracks 50 large companies. India VIX is tiny on purpose: it is a mood gauge, not a market you invest in.
One picture, the whole market. Instead of reading 18 numbers, you see everything at once. Mostly green? A good day. Mostly red? A tough one.
Tap any box. Tap a box to know more — a plain-English line about what it means. Try it — tap the gold-outlined box.
